BiblicalUsage: Shaçaç is the work of spoilers, stripping the fallen of everything they own. After David struck down Goliath, Israel returned and spoiled the tents of the Philistines. But the same word turns against Israel itself, for when they forsook the LORD He delivered them into the hands of spoilers, and the psalmist laments that every passer-by spoils His vine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe plunder follows idolatry like night follows day, because when Israel kept the LORD they spoiled their enemies, and when they left Him they were spoiled themselves.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
